independent.recovered_law: In Text A, it is humans (ἄνθρωποι) who seek death and death that flees from them — the mortal agent pursues and the abstraction withdraws. In Text B, it is voices/demands (φωναί/ἀπαιτήσεις) that pursue an answer which stays silent — the seeking agent is linguistic/juridical and the withdrawing abstraction is response rather than death.
independent.law_match_note: Both describe the same directional reversal: the pursuer/demander changes from human-seeking-death to demand-seeking-response, and the evader changes from death to silence/non-response — the relational inversion is identical.
independent.terminal_note: The final portion of Text B (9:9) maintains the substituted relation — demands/claims rushing into emptiness, weights pressing without relief — and does not revert to Text A's human-seeking-death structure.
